subject: general
question: Import substitution strategy is commonly called _________.
solution:
The correct answer is **"**__**Inward looking trade strategy.**__**"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Import substitution strategy** refers to a government policy aimed at promoting **domestic production** by substituting imported goods with domestically produced goods.
 
• Import substitution strategy is also known as **inward looking trade strategy **which aims to produce goods domestically which are imported to our nation.
 
• This strategy involves **imposing tariffs** and other trade barriers on** imported goods** to make them more expensive and less competitive in the domestic market.
 
• The** goal** of import substitution is to **reduce a country's reliance on imports **and build up its domestic industries, which can lead to economic growth and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Make in India campaign**," is a government initiative to promote **manufacturing and investment** in India.

 
 
• The **Prime Minister** introduced the Made in India program in **September 2014 **as a component of a larger series of nation-building programs.
 
 
 
• "**Outward looking trade strategy**," refers to a policy of** promoting exports** and opening up to international trade.
 
 
• The widely recognized definition of the **outward-oriented trade strategy** based on price incentives is when the** effective exchange rate** (EERx) of the nation is lower than its **import rate** (EERm).
 
 
 
• "**Balanced trade strategy**," refers to a policy of maintaining a **balance between imports and exports**.
 
 
• **Controlling inflation **and **enforcing tariffs** or other barriers, including **import certificates**, on a country-by-country basis are two ways to implement balanced trade.
